title: Reading the passé simple: il fut, elle prit
summary: Recognise the literary past tense of novels, tales and history books: the regular endings, the irregular forms you meet most, and how it shares a story with the imparfait.
focus: Recognising the passé simple in written stories, especially the il and ils forms
content:
## Why you meet the passé simple

The **passé simple** is the past tense of written stories: novels, fairy tales, history books, biographies and articles about the distant past. In conversation, French uses the **passé composé** for the same job, so you will rarely say it, but you must **recognise** it to read.

- **Il était une fois une reine qui avait trois filles.** (Once upon a time there was a queen who had three daughters.)
- **Napoléon naquit en Corse en 1769.** (Napoleon was born in Corsica in 1769.)
- spoken: **Je suis né en 2001.** (I was born in 2001.)

Stories are mostly told in the third person, so the **il / elle** and **ils / elles** forms are the ones you will meet most.

## The regular endings

Take the infinitive, drop **-er**, **-ir** or **-re**, and add:

| | parler | finir | vendre |
|---|---|---|---|
| je | parlai | finis | vendis |
| tu | parlas | finis | vendis |
| il / elle | parla | finit | vendit |
| nous | parlâmes | finîmes | vendîmes |
| vous | parlâtes | finîtes | vendîtes |
| ils / elles | parlèrent | finirent | vendirent |

Only **nous** and **vous** carry a circumflex. Spelling keeps the sound before **a**: **il commença**, **il mangea**. **Aller** is regular here: **il alla**, **ils allèrent**. An ending in **-èrent** or **-irent** always means *they did*.

## The irregular forms to recognise

Many irregular verbs take **-us, -us, -ut, -ûmes, -ûtes, -urent**; others take the **-is** set on a new stem; **venir** has its own **-ins** set.

| infinitive | il / elle | ils / elles |
|---|---|---|
| être | fut | furent |
| avoir | eut | eurent |
| pouvoir | put | purent |
| savoir | sut | surent |
| mourir | mourut | moururent |
| faire | fit | firent |
| prendre | prit | prirent |
| dire | dit | dirent |
| voir | vit | virent |
| mettre | mit | mirent |
| naître | naquit | naquirent |
| venir | vint | vinrent |

Watch the look-alikes: **il finit** and **il dit** are also present tense, and **il vit** is **voir** here but **vivre** in the present. The context decides.

## Passé simple and imparfait in a story

A written story shares out the work just as speech does with the passé composé:

- **passé simple**: the events, one after another. **Le loup frappa à la porte.** (The wolf knocked at the door.)
- **imparfait**: the background, descriptions and habits. **Il faisait nuit et la petite fille dormait.** (It was night and the little girl was asleep.)

> Il faisait froid. La forêt était silencieuse. Soudain, un cri retentit : le prince sauta de son cheval et courut vers le château.

(It was cold. The forest was silent. Suddenly a cry rang out: the prince jumped off his horse and ran to the castle.)

vocabulary.example: Il était une fois une petite fille qui vivait près d'une forêt.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Once upon a time there was a little girl who lived near a forest.

vocabulary.example: Ma grand-mère me lisait un conte chaque soir.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My grandmother used to read me a tale every evening.

vocabulary.example: Dans ce roman, le héros quitta Paris à vingt ans.
vocabulary.example_meaning: In this novel, the hero left Paris at twenty.

vocabulary.example: Le récit de son voyage fut publié en 1850.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The account of his journey was published in 1850.

vocabulary.example: Marie Curie naquit à Varsovie en 1867.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw in 1867.

vocabulary.example: Le petit garçon devint un grand musicien.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The little boy became a great musician.

vocabulary.meaning: to run away, to flee (il s'enfuit)
vocabulary.example: Le voleur prit l'argent et s'enfuit.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The thief took the money and ran away.

vocabulary.example: Ce château fut construit au seizième siècle.
vocabulary.example_meaning: This castle was built in the sixteenth century.

vocabulary.example: Soudain, quelqu'un frappa à la porte.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Suddenly, someone knocked at the door.

quiz.prompt: In a novel you read: 'Il prit son manteau et sortit.' Prit is the passé simple of…
quiz.explanation: Prendre has the passé simple il prit, ils prirent. Prier is regular (il pria) and partir gives il partit.

quiz.prompt: Ils ___ toute la nuit au coin du feu. (parler, passé simple)
quiz.explanation: -er verbs take -èrent in the ils form: ils parlèrent (they talked).

quiz.prompt: Le roi ___ très surpris par la nouvelle. Which passé simple of être fills the gap?
quiz.explanation: Être gives il fut, ils furent. Fit is faire and eut is avoir.

quiz.prompt: The passé simple of finir has the same il form as the present: il finit.
quiz.explanation: Il finit is both présent and passé simple; only the context tells them apart. The plural differs: ils finissent (présent) but ils finirent (passé simple).

quiz.prompt: Victor Hugo ___ à Besançon en 1802. (naître, passé simple)
quiz.explanation: Naître has an irregular stem in the passé simple: il naquit, ils naquirent. In speech you would say il est né.

quiz.prompt: Il ___ nuit quand le prince arriva au château. Which tense sets the scene?
quiz.explanation: The background (night, weather, descriptions) is in the imparfait; the event, arriva, is in the passé simple.
hints: Is the night an event or the backdrop?

quiz.prompt: 'Ils vinrent nous voir le lendemain.' Vinrent is the passé simple of ___ (write the infinitive).
quiz.explanation: Venir has its own -ins set: il vint, ils vinrent. They came to see us the next day.
hints: Think of il vient in the present.

quiz.prompt: French speakers use the passé simple to tell a friend what they did last weekend.
quiz.explanation: In speech the passé composé does that job: j'ai vu un film. The passé simple belongs to written narration.

quiz.prompt: In a history book: 'Louis XIV ___ à Versailles en 1715.' Which form is the passé simple of mourir?
quiz.explanation: Mourir takes the -us set: il mourut, ils moururent. Mourait is the imparfait, and mourit does not exist.
hints: Mourir sounds like the -us verbs: il fut, il put…

conversations.title: A strange verb in a novel
conversations.scenario: Tom, an English student in Lyon, asks his landlady Mme Girard about the book he is reading.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Madame Girard, je lis un roman, mais je ne comprends pas ce verbe.
lines.meaning: Mrs Girard, I'm reading a novel, but I don't understand this verb.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Montrez-moi. Ah, il fut : c'est le passé simple du verbe être.
lines.meaning: Show me. Ah, il fut: it's the passé simple of the verb être.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Le passé simple ? On ne l'utilise pas à l'oral ?
lines.meaning: The passé simple? Don't people use it when speaking?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Presque jamais. À l'oral, on dit il a été ; dans un roman, on écrit il fut.
lines.meaning: Hardly ever. When speaking we say il a été; in a novel we write il fut.
lines.note: passé composé in speech, passé simple in writing

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: And prirent, which verb is that?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: C'est prendre. Ils prirent le train veut dire ils ont pris le train.
lines.meaning: It's prendre. Ils prirent le train means they took the train.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pourquoi l'auteur écrit il faisait nuit, et pas il fit nuit ?
lines.meaning: Why does the author write il faisait nuit, and not il fit nuit?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Parce que c'est le décor. Le passé simple raconte, l'imparfait décrit.
lines.meaning: Because it's the backdrop. The passé simple tells, the imparfait describes.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Donc il faisait nuit, et soudain, le héros partit.
lines.meaning: So it was night, and suddenly the hero left.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Exactement ! Vous lisez déjà comme un vrai lecteur.
lines.meaning: Exactly! You already read like a real reader.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Merci ! Je vais finir le chapitre ce soir.
lines.meaning: Thanks! I'm going to finish the chapter tonight.

listening.text: Il était une fois un vieux roi.
listening.meaning: Once upon a time there was an old king.

listening.text: Le prince ouvrit la porte et entra.
listening.meaning: The prince opened the door and went in.
listening.note: Passé simple: ouvrir gives il ouvrit.

listening.text: Ils partirent avant le lever du soleil.
listening.note: New word: le lever du soleil = sunrise.

listening.text: La reine eut une fille au printemps.
listening.meaning: The queen had a daughter in the spring.
listening.note: Eut is avoir in the passé simple.

listening.text: Soudain, le loup sortit de la forêt.
listening.meaning: Suddenly, the wolf came out of the forest.
listening.note: New word: le loup = the wolf.

listening.text: Elle prit la lettre et la lut en silence.
listening.meaning: She took the letter and read it in silence.

listening.text: Quand la guerre finit, les soldats rentrèrent chez eux.
listening.meaning: When the war ended, the soldiers went back home.

listening.text: Il faisait froid, la neige tombait, et l'enfant s'endormit près du feu.
listening.meaning: It was cold, the snow was falling, and the child fell asleep by the fire.
listening.note: New word: s'endormir = to fall asleep.

guide.tip: Read the endings like a code: -a, -it, -ut, -int is one person (he, she); -èrent, -irent, -urent, -inrent is several (they).

concept.title: Hearing it in an audiobook
concept.markdown: Read aloud, **il parla** ends in an open *a* sound and **il parlait** in an *è* sound, so the two are easy to hear apart. **Je parlai** and **je parlais** are much closer: another reason the passé simple lives mostly in the third person.

bites.title: A written tense
bites.rule: The passé simple tells finished events in novels, tales and history books. In speech the passé composé does the same job.

bites.title: Irregulars to spot
bites.rule: il fut (être), il eut (avoir), il fit (faire), il prit (prendre), il vit (voir), il vint (venir), il naquit (naître), il mourut (mourir).
bites.example_meaning: The weather was fine that day.

bites.title: Events and scene
bites.rule: Passé simple for the events of a story, imparfait for the background and descriptions.
bites.example_meaning: It was raining when she arrived.

sorts.title: Passé simple or imparfait?
sorts.why: The imparfait always ends in -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient; the passé simple has its own endings: -a, -it, -ut, -âmes, -îmes, -èrent, -irent.

sorts.title: Which infinitive?
sorts.why: Être and avoir take the -us set (fut, eut); faire takes the -is set on a short stem (fit).

spots.sentence: Le prince ouvra la porte du château.
spots.why: Ouvrir has -er endings in the present but -is endings in the passé simple: il ouvrit.

spots.sentence: Ils parlarent longtemps avec le roi.
spots.why: -er verbs take -èrent in the ils form: ils parlèrent.

spots.sentence: Elle prenit son sac et partit.
spots.why: Prendre has a short stem in the passé simple: elle prit.
Venir has its own -ins set: ils vinrent.

spots.sentence: Il mettit son chapeau et sortit.
spots.why: Mettre gives il mit, ils mirent.

builds.text: Elle prit sa valise et partit.
builds.meaning: She took her suitcase and left.

builds.text: Il faisait froid quand elle arriva.
builds.meaning: It was cold when she arrived.
